areas.name: Orthogonal polynomials, Jacobi matrices and Gauss-type quadrature
areas.title: Orthogonal polynomials, Jacobi matrices and Gauss-type quadrature
areas.summary: Orthogonal polynomials of a measure (general and spectral), zeros and interlacing, Christoffel numbers, Gauss, Radau and Lobatto rules and their remainders, kernel polynomials and modifications, moments and the modified Chebyshev algorithm (Gautschi 2004).

results.title: Monic orthogonal polynomials of a measure on ℝ: existence, uniqueness, finite case
results.informal: For a finite positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R$ with finite moments, $(p,q)_\mu=\int pq\,d\mu$ is positive definite on $\mathcal P_n$ iff $\mu$ has at least $n+1$ support points; then Gram–Schmidt on $1,t,\dots,t^n$ gives the unique monic $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_n$ with $\deg\pi_k=k$ and $(\pi_k,\pi_l)_\mu=0$ ($k\ne l$), $\|\pi_k\|_\mu>0$. If $\mu$ has exactly $N$ support points there are exactly $N$ of them and the Gram–Schmidt $\pi_N$ is the node polynomial (norm $0$). For $\mu=\mu_b$ they are $\det(xI-T_k)$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ a finite positive measure on $\mathbb R$ with $\int|t|^k\,d\mu<\infty$ for all $k$ (e.g. compact support)
$n\in\mathbb N$ with $\#\operatorname{supp}\mu\ge n+1$
results.conclusion: There exist unique monic $\pi_0,\dots,\pi_n\in\mathbb R[X]$, $\deg\pi_k=k$, $\int\pi_k\pi_l\,d\mu=0$ for $k\ne l$ and $\int\pi_k^2\,d\mu>0$; any $p$ with $\deg p\le n$ orthogonal to all of them is $0$; for $\#\operatorname{supp}\mu=N$ the inner product is not positive definite on $\mathcal P_N$; for $\mu=\mu_b$, $\pi_k=\det(xI-T_k)$ for $k\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: abstract Gram–Schmidt; needs the inner product on ℝ[X] (or degreeLT) induced by μ
Mathlib only has specific families (Chebyshev T orthogonal for measureT)

results.notes: Lets every statement of Gautschi Ch. 1 be made for a general measure (Chebyshev `measureT`, limiting spectral densities) instead of only for $\mu_b$; the bridge lemma $\pi_k(\cdot;\mu_b)=\det(xI-T_k)$ connects to `lanczos-orthogonal-polynomials`. Consumers: all candidates below stated for general $\mu$, spectral density estimation, KPM. Prove (Gram–Schmidt + `Polynomial.Sequence`).

results.title: Hankel moment matrices: positivity criterion and determinantal formulas
results.informal: With $M_n=[\mu_{i+j}]_{i,j<n}$ and $\Delta_n=\det M_n$: $(\cdot,\cdot)_\mu$ is positive definite on $\mathcal P_{n-1}$ iff $M_n\succ0$ iff $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_n>0$. For $\mu_b$, $M_n=K_n^\top K_n$ with $K_n=[b,Ab,\dots,A^{n-1}b]$, so $M_n\succ0$ iff $n\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$. Moreover $\pi_k$ is $\Delta_k^{-1}$ times the Hankel determinant with last row $(1,t,\dots,t^k)$, $\alpha_k=\Delta'_{k+1}/\Delta_{k+1}-\Delta'_k/\Delta_k$, $\beta_k=\Delta_{k+1}\Delta_{k-1}/\Delta_k^2$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ a positive measure with finite moments $\mu_r=\int t^r\,d\mu$
$\Delta'_k$ the Hankel determinant of order $k+1$ with its penultimate column and last row deleted
results.conclusion: $\int p^2\,d\mu=c^\top M_{d+1}c$ for $p=\sum c_kt^k$; positive definiteness on $\mathcal P_d$ iff $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_{d+1}>0$; determinantal formulas for $\pi_k$, $\alpha_k$, $\beta_k$; $M_n(\mu_b)=K_n^\top K_n$.

mathlib_prereqs.decl: Sylvester's criterion (PosDef iff leading minors positive)
mathlib_prereqs.note: not in Mathlib; NLAlib `card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_sign_changes` (sylvester-inertia) is the route

results.notes: Consumers: grade characterisation via moment matrices, moment-based spectral density estimation (and its ill-conditioning), `formal-orthogonal-polynomials`. Prove.

results.title: Zeros of orthogonal polynomials: simple, interior, strictly interlacing, one per gap; Gauss weights positive
aliases: unreduced Jacobi matrix has simple eigenvalues
at most one Ritz value per spectral gap
results.informal:
For symmetric $A$, $b$ with grade $
u$ and the Lanczos $T_q$ ($1\le q\le
u$): the eigenvalues of $T_q$ (zeros of $\pi_q(\cdot;\mu_b)$) are simple; for $q<
u$ they lie in the open interval $(\min\operatorname{supp}\mu_b,\max\operatorname{supp}\mu_b)$; for $q<
u$ the eigenvalues of $T_q$ strictly interlace those of $T_{q+1}$; an open interval containing no point of $\operatorname{supp}\mu_b$ contains at most one eigenvalue of $T_q$; every Gauss weight $(e_1^	op u_i)^2$ is strictly positive. Same statements for $\pi_n(\cdot;\mu)$ of a general measure with $>n$ support points.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ symmetric, $b\ne0$, $\nu=\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$, $\mu_b=\sum_i (u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ the spectral measure of symmetric $A$ and $b$ (`NLAlib.spectralMeasure`)
$T_q$ the Jacobi matrix of a Lanczos decomposition of size $q\le\nu$ (positive off-diagonal)
results.notes: NLAlib has non-strict interlacing and nodes in the closed spectral interval; this closes the gap noted in `jacobi-matrix-identities` (strict interlacing open). Route: an eigenvector of an unreduced tridiagonal matrix has nonzero first component (it is $\tilde\pi(\theta)$, Thm 1.31), giving simplicity and positive weights; the confluent Christoffel–Darboux inequality gives strict interlacing; orthogonality of $\pi_q$ against $\pi_q/((t-\tau_i)(t-\tau_j))$ gives one zero per gap. Consumers: `lanczos-fa-interpolation` (distinct Ritz values), `ritz-value-bounds`, `slq-error` (positive weights), `cg-finite-termination`. Prove.

results.title: Jacobi eigenvectors, Christoffel numbers and discrete orthogonality
results.informal: For $\mu_b$ and $q\le\nu$ with orthonormal Lanczos polynomials $p_0,\dots,p_{q-1}$: $T_q\,\mathbf p(\theta_i)=\theta_i\,\mathbf p(\theta_i)$ with $\mathbf p=(p_0,\dots,p_{q-1})^\top$, so $u_i=\pm\mathbf p(\theta_i)/\|\mathbf p(\theta_i)\|$ and the Gauss weight is $\|b\|^2(e_1^\top u_i)^2=1/\sum_{k<q}p_k(\theta_i)^2$; the first $q$ orthonormal polynomials are orthonormal for the Gauss rule: $\sum_iw_ip_k(\theta_i)p_l(\theta_i)=\delta_{kl}$.
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric, $\mu_b=\sum_i (u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ the spectral measure of symmetric $A$ and $b$ (`NLAlib.spectralMeasure`)
Lanczos decomposition of size $q\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$ with eigenpairs $(\theta_i,u_i)$ of $T_q$
results.notes: Eigenvalue half of Thm 1.31 is in NLAlib (`integral_eval_charpoly_mul_eq_zero`); this adds the eigenvector and weight formulas. Consumers: `orthogonal-polynomial-zeros` (positive weights), `gauss-radau-lobatto`, SLQ weight analysis, Ritz-vector first components in Lanczos-FA error formulas. Prove (difficulty 2: evaluate `X_mul_poly` at a zero of $\det(xI-T_q)$).

results.title: Gauss quadrature remainder in derivative form (Markov); sign-definite Lanczos quadrature errors
results.informal: The $n$-point Gauss sum equals $\int H_{2n-1}f\,d\mu$, the integral of the Hermite interpolant of $f,f'$ at the nodes; hence for $f\in C^{2n}[a,b]$ ($[a,b]\supseteq\operatorname{supp}\mu$), $\int f\,d\mu-\sum\lambda_\nu f(\tau_\nu)=\frac{f^{(2n)}(\xi)}{(2n)!}\int\pi_n^2\,d\mu$. Matrix form: $b^\top f(A)b-\|b\|^2e_1^\top f(T_q)e_1=\frac{f^{(2q)}(\xi)}{(2q)!}\|\chi_q(A)b\|^2$ with $\chi_q=\det(xI-T_q)$, so the Lanczos value is a lower bound whenever $f^{(2q)}\ge0$ on the spectral interval (e.g. $f=1/x,\,x^{-2}$ on $(0,\infty)$; an upper bound for $\log$).
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric with spectrum in $[a,c]$, $\mu_b=\sum_i (u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ the spectral measure of symmetric $A$ and $b$ (`NLAlib.spectralMeasure`)
Lanczos decomposition of size $q\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$, $T_q$, $\chi_q=\det(xI-T_q)$
$f\in C^{2q}[a,c]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: neither Mathlib nor NLAlib; NLAlib has the Lagrange remainder `exists_sub_eval_interpolate_eq` (distinct nodes) to be extended to doubled nodes

results.notes: Complements NLAlib's approximation-based error bounds with the classical sign-definite remainder. Consumers: CG error estimation ($\|x-x_k\|_A^2=r_0^\top A^{-1}r_0-\dots$ lower bounds, Ex 3.46), `diagonal-estimator` / trace-of-inverse bounds (Ex 3.47), log-determinant bounds in SLQ (`slq-error`), `gauss-radau-lobatto`. Needs Hermite interpolation remainder (difficulty 3). Prove; could be assumed first (statement certain).

results.title: Gauss–Radau and Gauss–Lobatto rules via bordered Jacobi matrices; two-sided bounds for bᵀf(A)b
results.informal: Radau: bordering $T_q$ by $\beta_qe_q$ with corner $\alpha^R=a-\beta_q^2\chi_{q-1}(a)/\chi_q(a)$ gives $\hat T_{q+1}$ with eigenvalue $a$ whose Golub–Welsch rule is exact to degree $2q$ and has remainder $\frac{f^{(2q+1)}(\xi)}{(2q+1)!}\int(t-a)\chi_q^2(\cdot;\mu_b^a)\,d\mu_b$; so if $f^{(2q+1)}$ has constant sign on $[a,c]$ the Radau values at $a$ and at $c$ bracket $b^\top f(A)b$. Lobatto: a bordered $(q+2)\times(q+2)$ matrix with eigenvalues $a,c$ (corner and coupling from a $2\times2$ system) is exact to degree $2q+1$ with remainder of sign $-\operatorname{sgn}f^{(2q+2)}$. Applications: two-sided bounds for $\|x-x_k\|_2^2=r^\top A^{-2}r$, $\|x-x_k\|_A^2=r^\top A^{-1}r$ and $(A^{-1})_{ii}$; Lobatto discrete orthogonality (Thm 1.23); the Chebyshev Gauss–Lobatto rule (Ex 1.50).
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric with spectrum in $[a,c]$ ($a$, $c$ not necessarily eigenvalues), $\mu_b=\sum_i (u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ the spectral measure of symmetric $A$ and $b$ (`NLAlib.spectralMeasure`)
Lanczos decomposition of size $q+1\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$
results.conclusion: Radau and Lobatto rules from the bordered matrices are exact to degrees $2q$, $2q+1$; remainders have the stated derivative forms; for $f^{(2q+1)}>0$ (resp. $f^{(2q+2)}>0$) on $[a,c]$ the left Radau value is an upper bound, the right Radau a lower bound, and Lobatto an upper bound (signs flip with the derivative).

mathlib_prereqs.note: Gauss–Chebyshev; the Lobatto–Chebyshev analogue is absent

results.notes: Consumers: `diagonal-estimator` (deterministic bounds on $(A^{-1})_{ii}$), CG stopping criteria and error estimation (`cg-convergence`), log-determinant / trace bounds in SLQ (`slq-error`), Bai–Golub bounds. Source also: Golub–Meurant (2010) Ch. 6–7. Prove after `gauss-quadrature-derivative-remainder`.

results.title: Kernel polynomials: orthogonal polynomials of (t−z)dμ, the qd/LR step on the Jacobi matrix, and the CG direction polynomials
results.informal: If $\pi_k(z)\ne0$ for all $k$, $\hat\pi_n(t;z)=\big(\pi_{n+1}(t)-\tfrac{\pi_{n+1}(z)}{\pi_n(z)}\pi_n(t)\big)/(t-z)$ are the monic orthogonal polynomials of $(t-z)\,d\mu$; with $q_k=-\pi_{k+1}(z)/\pi_k(z)$ and $e_k$ from $\alpha_k=z+q_k+e_{k-1}$, $\beta_k=e_{k-1}q_{k-1}$, their coefficients are $\hat\alpha_k=z+q_k+e_k$, $\hat\beta_k=q_ke_{k-1}$. Matrix form: $J_n-zI=LU$ (bidiagonal, no pivoting) and $UL+zI$ is the Jacobi matrix of $(t-z)\,d\mu$. For real $z$ outside the support (and positive $\mu$) all quantities are well defined. For SPD $A$, $z=0$, $\mu=\mu_{r_0}$: these are the CG search-direction polynomials ($A$-conjugacy is orthogonality for $t\,d\mu$) and $T_k=LDL^\top$ carries the CG coefficients.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive (or quasi-definite) with recurrence coefficients $\alpha_k,\beta_k$
$z\in\mathbb C$ with $\pi_k(z)\ne0$ for all relevant $k$ (automatic for real $z$ outside the support interval)
results.notes: The orthogonal-polynomial content of the CG–Lanczos equivalence. Consumers: `cg-recurrence` (Hestenes–Stiefel coefficients from $T_k=LDL^\top$), `cg-convergence`, `preconditioned-cg`, shifted systems. Prove.

results.title: Quasi-definite measures and formal orthogonal polynomials
results.informal: A real or complex measure (moment functional) is quasi-definite if all Hankel determinants are nonzero; then and only then there is a unique sequence of monic formal orthogonal polynomials, and they satisfy a three-term recurrence with $\beta_k\ne0$.
hypotheses: a linear functional $L$ on $\mathbb C[X]$ (moments $\mu_r=L(t^r)$)
results.conclusion: monic formal orthogonal polynomials exist and are unique iff $\Delta_n\ne0$ for all $n$; they satisfy $\pi_{k+1}=(t-\alpha_k)\pi_k-\beta_k\pi_{k-1}$ with $\beta_k\ne0$.
results.notes: Consumer: two-sided (nonsymmetric) Lanczos and BiCG breakdown theory (no atlas entry yet). Prove.

results.notes: Extends NLAlib's real-$x$ continued-fraction identity to complex $z$ (listed open in `jacobi-matrix-identities`). Consumers: resolvent quadratic forms $b^\top(zI-A)^{-1}b$, spectral density via the Stieltjes transform / Stieltjes–Perron, `rational-gauss-quadrature`. Prove.

results.title: Symmetric measures: parity of orthogonal polynomials and reduction to t² (Lanczos on the augmented matrix vs AᵀA)
results.informal: If $\mu$ is symmetric about $0$ then $\alpha_k=0$ and $\pi_k(-t)=(-1)^k\pi_k(t)$; writing $\pi_{2k}(t)=\pi^+_k(t^2)$, $\pi_{2k+1}(t)=t\pi^-_k(t^2)$, $\pi^+_k$ and $\pi^-_k$ are the monic orthogonal polynomials of the push-forwards of $\mu$ and $t^2\mu$ under $t\mapsto t^2$. Matrix form: for $M=\begin{bmatrix}0&B\\B^\top&0\end{bmatrix}$ and start $(u,0)$, $\mu$ is symmetric, and the even/odd Lanczos polynomials are those of the spectral measures of $(BB^\top,u)$ and $(B^\top B,B^\top u)$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ a positive measure invariant under $t\mapsto-t$ (e.g. the spectral measure of the augmented matrix and $(u,0)$)
results.notes: Consumers: `golub-kahan-bidiagonalization` (bidiagonal $B_k$ from Lanczos on the augmented matrix), `cgls-lsqr-bound`, singular-value quadrature $u^\top f(BB^\top)u$. Prove.

results.title: Bounds on the recurrence coefficients of a compactly supported measure
results.informal: If $\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq[a,b]$ (with more than $k+1$ points) then $a<\alpha_k<b$ and $0<\beta_k\le\max(a^2,b^2)$. Matrix form: the Lanczos coefficients satisfy $\lambda_{\min}(A)\le\alpha_j\le\lambda_{\max}(A)$ and $0<\beta_j\le\|A\|_2$ below the grade.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with support in $[a,b]$; $k$ below the number of support points minus one
results.notes: Positivity of $\beta_j$ is already proved (`LanczosDecomp.beta_arnoldiDecomp_pos`). Consumers: a-priori bounds on $T_q$ (finite-precision Lanczos analysis, `ritz-value-bounds`). Prove (routine).

results.title: Monic recurrence for det(xI − T_j), norm products, monic and confluent Christoffel–Darboux
results.informal: For $\chi_j=\det(xI-T_j)$ ($\chi_0=1$, $\chi_{-1}=0$): $\chi_{j+1}=(x-\alpha_j)\chi_j-\beta_j^2\chi_{j-1}$; $\int\chi_j^2\,d\mu_b=\|b\|^2\beta_1^2\cdots\beta_j^2$, $\alpha_j=\int t\chi_j^2\,d\mu_b/\int\chi_j^2\,d\mu_b$, $\beta_j^2=\int\chi_j^2/\int\chi_{j-1}^2$; monic Christoffel–Darboux $\sum_{k\le n}\big(\prod_{i=k+1}^n\beta_i^2\big)\chi_k(x)\chi_k(y)=\frac{\chi_{n+1}(x)\chi_n(y)-\chi_n(x)\chi_{n+1}(y)}{x-y}$ and the confluent form $\sum_{k<m}p_k(x)^2=\beta_m(p_m'(x)p_{m-1}(x)-p_{m-1}'(x)p_m(x))>0$; $\chi_k$ are the denominators $B_k$ of the Jacobi continued fraction.
hypotheses: $A$ symmetric, $\mu_b=\sum_i (u_i^\top b)^2\delta_{\lambda_i}$ the spectral measure of symmetric $A$ and $b$ (`NLAlib.spectralMeasure`)
Lanczos decomposition of size $q\le\operatorname{grade}(A,b)$ with coefficients $\alpha_j,\beta_j$ (NLAlib indexing, $\beta_j=t_{j,j-1}$)
results.conclusion: the three-term monic recurrence, the norm and quotient formulas, the monic and confluent Christoffel–Darboux identities, and $B_k=\chi_k$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: Laplace expansion for the leading-minor recurrence

results.notes: Closes the 'partial' gaps on Thms 1.27, 1.32, Cor 1.32 and 1.34. Consumers: `gauss-quadrature-derivative-remainder` (the constant $\int\chi_q^2$), `orthogonal-polynomial-zeros` (confluent CD gives strict interlacing), Sturm counts (`sylvester-inertia`: the leading minors of $T-xI$ are $\pm\chi_j$), CG error formulas. Prove.

results.title: Continuity of recurrence coefficients and Gauss rules under convergence of moments
results.informal: If measures $\mu_N$ and $\mu$ on $[a,b]$ satisfy $\int p\,d\mu_N\to\int p\,d\mu$ for every polynomial and $\mu$ has more than $n$ support points, then $\alpha_k(\mu_N)\to\alpha_k(\mu)$, $\beta_k(\mu_N)\to\beta_k(\mu)$ for $k<n$, $\pi_n(\cdot;\mu_N)\to\pi_n(\cdot;\mu)$ uniformly on $[a,b]$, and the $n$-point Gauss nodes and weights converge.
hypotheses: $\mu_N,\mu$ positive measures supported in a fixed compact $[a,b]$
moment convergence $\int t^k\,d\mu_N\to\int t^k\,d\mu$ for all $k$
$\#\operatorname{supp}\mu>n$
results.notes: Consumers: spectral-density estimation (averaged/limiting spectral measures, SLQ vs KPM), stability of Lanczos coefficients under perturbation of the moments. Prove.

results.title: Contour-integral representation of the Gauss remainder for analytic integrands
aliases: Gauss quadrature error for analytic functions
results.informal: For $\mu$ supported in $[a,b]$ and $f$ analytic on a domain containing $[a,b]$, $R_n^G(f)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma K_n(z)f(z)\,dz$ with $K_n=\rho_n/\pi_n$, $\rho_n(z)=\int\pi_n(t)\,d\mu(t)/(z-t)$, for any contour $\Gamma$ in the domain encircling $[a,b]$; hence $|R_n^G(f)|\le\frac{\ell(\Gamma)}{2\pi}\max_\Gamma|K_n|\max_\Gamma|f|$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with support in $[a,b]$
$f$ holomorphic on an open set containing a closed contour $\Gamma$ that winds once around $[a,b]$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Cauchy integral formula machinery for circles; general contours/ellipses need more

results.notes: Alternative to the Chebyshev/Bernstein-ellipse route used by `lanczos-quadrature-analytic-error`; gives sharper, measure-dependent constants. Consumer: `slq-error`. Prove or assume.

results.title: Derivatives of recurrence coefficients with respect to (modified) moments
aliases: sensitivity of Jacobi matrix to moments
condition of the moment map K_n
results.informal: For modified moments $m_k=\int p_k\,d\mu$ ($p_k$ a basis of $\mathcal P_{2n-1}$, $c_k[q]$ the coordinates of $q$): $\partial_{m_k}\int q\,d\mu=c_k[q]+\int\partial_{m_k}q\,d\mu$, and $\partial\alpha_j/\partial m_k=c_k[\tilde\psi_{2j+1}]$, $\partial\beta_j/\partial m_k=c_k[\tilde\psi_{2j}]$ with $\tilde\psi_{2j}=\beta_j(\tilde\pi_j^2-\tilde\pi_{j-1}^2)$, $\tilde\psi_{2j+1}=\sqrt{\beta_{j+1}}\tilde\pi_j\tilde\pi_{j+1}-\sqrt{\beta_j}\tilde\pi_{j-1}\tilde\pi_j$; the condition number of $m\mapsto(\alpha,\beta)$ is the norm of $[c_k[\tilde\psi_l]]$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with more than $n$ support points
$p_0,\dots,p_{2n-1}$ a basis of $\mathcal P_{2n-1}$
results.notes: Consumers: perturbation of Lanczos coefficients under perturbed spectral measures (finite-precision Lanczos, noisy moments in KPM/SLQ). Prove.

For $f:\mathbb R^m	o\mathbb R^n$ Fréchet differentiable at $x$: $\operatorname{cond}_{abs}f(x)=\|Df(x)\|$; componentwise relative condition matrix $C_{
u\mu}=x_\mu\partial_\mu f_
u(x)/f_
u(x)$ and $\operatorname{cond}_{rel}f(x)=\|C(x)\|$; scalar cases $|f'(x)|$ and $|xf'(x)/f(x)|$.

results.conclusion: definitions, with $\operatorname{cond}_{rel}$ of $x\mapsto Ax$ bounded by $\kappa(A)$-type quantities.
results.notes: NLAlib has only the matrix condition number. Consumers: `recurrence-coefficient-moment-sensitivity`, perturbation statements in matrix-conditioning. Prove (definitions).

results.title: Modified Chebyshev algorithm: Jacobi matrix from modified moments
results.informal: Given monic $p_k$ with $p_{k+1}=(t-a_k)p_k-b_kp_{k-1}$ and modified moments $m_k=\int p_k\,d\mu$ ($k<2n$), the mixed moments $\sigma_{kl}=\int\pi_kp_l\,d\mu$ satisfy $\sigma_{-1,l}=0$, $\sigma_{0,l}=m_l$, $\sigma_{kl}=\sigma_{k-1,l+1}-(\alpha_{k-1}-a_l)\sigma_{k-1,l}-\beta_{k-1}\sigma_{k-2,l}+b_l\sigma_{k-1,l-1}$, and $\alpha_0=a_0+m_1/m_0$, $\alpha_k=a_k-\sigma_{k-1,k}/\sigma_{k-1,k-1}+\sigma_{k,k+1}/\sigma_{kk}$, $\beta_k=\sigma_{kk}/\sigma_{k-1,k-1}$, $\beta_0=m_0$.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with more than $n$ support points
$p_k$ monic with a known three-term recurrence ($a_k\in\mathbb R$, $b_k\ge0$)

results.title: Clenshaw's algorithm for sums of three-term-recurrence sequences

results.title: Christoffel and Uvarov theorems: orthogonal polynomials of rationally modified measures
results.informal: For $d\hat\mu=(u/v)\,d\mu$ with $u,v$ coprime real polynomials with simple zeros, not vanishing on the support, $u\hat\pi_n$ is (up to a constant) the determinant with first row $\pi_{n-m},\dots,\pi_{n+\ell}$ ($\ell=\deg u$, $m=\deg v\le n$), rows of values $\pi_j(u_i)$ at the zeros of $u$ and rows of Cauchy integrals $\rho_j(v_i)$ at the zeros of $v$; a bordered variant holds for $m>n$. Special cases give the linear/quadratic factor and divisor algorithms, e.g. $\hat\pi_n=\pi_n+s_n\pi_{n-1}+t_n\pi_{n-2}$ for a quadratic divisor.
hypotheses: $\mu$ positive with support $[a,b]$
$u,v$ coprime with simple zeros outside $[a,b]$, $u/v>0$ on $[a,b]$
results.conclusion: determinantal formulas for $u\,\pi_n(\cdot;\hat\mu)$; recurrence coefficients of $\hat\mu$ computable from those of $\mu$ and $\rho_k$.
results.notes: Consumers: spectral measures modified by resolvents ($(t-z)^{-1}d\mu_b$: shifted systems, rational Krylov), Gauss rules for $f(t)/(t-z)$. Assume or prove the linear cases first.
